title: Quiz: Effect of Temperature on Rate

questions.stem: According to the general rule of thumb, what happens to the rate of reaction for every 10°C increase in temperature?

options.text: The rate halves
The rate approximately doubles
The rate stays the same
The rate increases by 10%

questions.explanation: As a general rule of thumb, for every 10°C rise in temperature, the rate of reaction approximately doubles. This shows that temperature has a dramatic effect on rate.

questions.stem: Temperature increases the rate of reaction for two reasons. Which is the MORE important reason?

options.text: Particles collide more frequently
A greater proportion of particles have energy equal to or greater than the activation energy
The activation energy decreases
Particles become smaller and collide more easily

questions.explanation: While higher temperature does increase collision frequency, the more important effect is that a greater proportion of particles have energy exceeding the activation energy, leading to more successful collisions.

questions.stem: What does a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve show?

options.text: The change in concentration over time
The distribution of energies among particles at a given temperature
The rate of reaction at different temperatures
The amount of product formed over time

questions.explanation: A Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve shows how the kinetic energies of particles in a sample are distributed at a particular temperature. It helps explain why temperature affects the rate.

questions.stem: On a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, what happens to the curve at a higher temperature?

options.text: The peak shifts to the right and becomes lower, with more particles exceeding the activation energy
The peak shifts to the left and becomes higher
The curve does not change shape
The activation energy line moves to the right

questions.explanation: At a higher temperature, the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve shifts to the right (higher average energy) and flattens. The area under the curve beyond the activation energy increases, meaning more particles can react.

questions.stem: Why does putting food in a refrigerator help it last longer?

options.text: The cold temperature kills all bacteria
Lower temperature slows down the rate of chemical reactions that cause food to spoil
The fridge removes oxygen from around the food
The cold increases the activation energy of decomposition reactions

questions.explanation: Refrigeration lowers the temperature, which slows down the chemical reactions and biological processes that cause food to decompose and spoil.

questions.stem: At a higher temperature, particles move faster. How does this contribute to an increased rate of reaction?

options.text: Faster particles are larger and react more easily
Faster particles collide more frequently, increasing the chance of successful collisions
Faster particles have lower activation energy
Faster particles change the orientation needed for a collision

questions.explanation: When particles move faster due to higher temperature, they collide more frequently. This increases the number of collisions per second, giving more opportunities for successful collisions.

questions.stem: Which experiment is commonly used to investigate the effect of temperature on reaction rate?

options.text: Electrolysis of copper sulfate solution
Sodium thiosulfate and hydrochloric acid (disappearing cross)
Chromatography of ink samples
Titration of an acid with an alkali

questions.explanation: The sodium thiosulfate and hydrochloric acid experiment (disappearing cross) is commonly used to investigate temperature effects because the reaction rate can be easily measured by timing how quickly the cross disappears at different temperatures.
